newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX sees Fri meet with Energy Sec "educational".
newsitem.headline: NYMEX sees Fri meet with Energy Sec "educational".

text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange president, Patrick Thompson, said Thursday he does not expect to agree on any initiatives to curb high heating oil prices when he meets U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary on Friday.
"I think it is going to be a real productive meeting" but its purpose is more educational and won't be on policy, Thompson told Reuters at a Futures Industry Association conference here.
Oil analysts have suggested that speculation in the futures markets has deepened the market's backwardation in which prices in near months are higher than the deferreds.
"It is a real opportunity for the exchange to explain its role in price formation and discuss some of the fundamentals in the market," Thompson said.

Referring to the backwardation in the oil markets, Thompson said: "Prices just don't make themselves. Some people have said because you have a backwardation in the oil market that that discourages the storage of oil."
"Whether or not we have a backwardated market,...whatever effect that has on storage...it is going to be with or without a futures market," he added.

Thompson's meeting with Secretary O'Leary follows an Energy Department meeting last Friday with oil executives after which a couple of refiners said they would try to speed up their production of heating oil.

Heating oil prices rose 50 percent to last week from July values as stocks dwindled to 20-year lows. However, figures this week showing a big build in heating oil stocks in the key U.S. Northeast market and a move by the Colonial Pipeline to open up more capacity to run heating oil from the Gulf of Mexico to the Northeast, eased prices somewhat.
After peaking at 76.30 cents a gallon earlier this month, heating oil futures slumped sharply Wednesday and Thursday to end at 70.49 cents.
